numbers_that_differ_by_source.note: Not reconciled. Nothing read this session explains the difference; do not merge or average.
Two of three sources say 104; the landing page says 100.

The manuscript's 57,180 is the sum of 49,080 neurons and glia and 8100 blood-vessel cells in the same sentence; the data page's 50k describes a cell-body layer. Whether 50k is the 49,080 rounded is the drafter's guess, not stated by any source.

must_not_imply: Not a whole brain: it is about one cubic millimetre, a slab 170 micrometres thick.
Not a wiring diagram of a person: it is one fragment, the reconstruction is automated, and the paper reports 104 proofread neurons (the landing page says 100 proofread cells).
One donor: nothing here generalises to people in general, and the card must not say 'the human brain contains'.

A surgical sample, not healthy-volunteer tissue: it was removed during surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy to reach the hippocampus (the paper states this). Do not call it diseased tissue either: the paper says it was judged normal by light microscopy and that subtle effects cannot be excluded.

Nothing about the donor's age or sex: neither appears in the published abstract, the two release pages or the main text of the author manuscript. The supplementary materials were not read. Do not state either from memory or from news coverage.
Nothing about which hemisphere: not found in the sources read.
The synapse counts are not exact and are not interchangeable: quote one figure with its source.
No link to any QIF region's function: H01 is anatomy at nanometre scale and makes no claim about what temporal cortex does.
No claim about consent or ethics approval wording: not read this session.
Do not say the whole dataset was made 'not by hand' or 'by computers alone': the manuscript says the cell census was manual.

card.title: One cubic millimetre, one patient

sentences.text: H01 is a map of about one cubic millimetre of human temporal cortex, imaged with an electron microscope at a resolution of 4 by 4 by 33 nanometres.
The tissue came from one patient with epilepsy: surgeons removed it to reach a deeper part of the brain.
The paper reports about 57,000 cells and about 150 million synapses in the sample, while the project's release page counts 183 million annotated synapses.
The reconstruction was made by automated methods, and the paper reports that 104 neurons were then proofread by people, so it is a fragment and not the wiring diagram of a brain or a person.
The data are free to reuse with attribution under a CC BY 4.0 licence and are described in Shapson-Coe et al., Science, 2024.

card.attribution_line: Shapson-Coe et al. (2024), Science 384(6696), doi:10.1126/science.adk4858. Data: H01 release, CC BY 4.0, https://h01-release.storage.googleapis.com/landing.html
card.drafting_notes: AI-drafted, then reworded in round 2 after an AI verifier's check. Sentence 1 gives the voxel size as the released-data page states it; the paper's own figure was not quoted. Sentence 4 uses the manuscript's count of 104 proofread neurons; the release landing page says 100 proofread cells. 'With attribution' in sentence 5 is what the licence name means; the page itself says only 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 License'.
